Combat Sequence

  1. Roll 1d6 for each side; the higher roll acts first.
  2. Check morale for NPCs and monsters.
  3. Move, then resolve missile fire, spells and hand-to-hand attacks.
  4. Apply damage and resolve special effects.

Attack: d20 + Strength/Dexterity + magic + mastery versus THAC0 - AC. Natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits automatically. Damage uses the weapon die plus Strength for melee attacks.

Attack Matrix

Read the row for the target's AC to find the needed modified d20 result. The dagger symbol marks an automatic hit on a natural 20; a natural 1 still misses.

Encounters and Reaction Rolls

Chance of encounter: in a dungeon or city, roll 1d6 every two turns (1d12 once at night); on a 1 an encounter occurs. In the wilderness, roll 1d6 by day and 1d12 at night: clear, grasslands, inhabited or settled land needs a 1; forest, river, hills, barren land, desert, ocean or aerial needs 1-2; swamp, jungle or mountains needs 1-3.

Surprise: both sides roll 1d6; a 1 or 2 means surprised. Both surprised loses a round for each side; one surprised gives the other a free round or automatic evasion; neither surprised gives no advantage. Surprise sets distance to 1d4 x 10 feet or yards, with the surprised side noticing at half distance when only one side is surprised.

Distance: without surprise, dungeon bright light is 4d6 x 10 ft, dim light 2d6 x 10 ft, darkness 1d4 x 10 ft; wilderness bright daylight 4d6 x 10 yards, dim light 2d6 x 10 yards, very poor visibility 1d4 x 10 yards. Ocean ships are detected at 300/120/40 yards by visibility and ocean monsters use 4d6/2d6/1d4 x 10 yards; undersea uses 1d6 x 10 yards. Wandering monsters in a dungeon appear 2d6 x 10 ft away.

Reactions: roll 2d6 on the Monster Reactions (2d6) table in the BECMI Tables compendium: 2-3 Monster attacks; 4-6 the monster is aggressive and you roll again in one round with a penalty of -4; 7-9 the monster is cautious and you roll again; 10-11 the monster is neutral and you roll again with a bonus of +4; 12 the monster is friendly. The first roll ignores Charisma; later rolls add Charisma, PC actions of -2 to +2 and the listed modifier. Never roll more than three times; a third roll below 10 means the monster attacks or leaves.

Which monsters: roll 1d20 on the Dungeon Encounters table for the current dungeon level, then roll the number appearing shown in that row. In the wilderness, roll 1d8 for the terrain column, then 1d12 on the indicated subtable. These are die rolls; the tables are consulted by column and are not random tables in the compendium.

Evasion and pursuit: compare party size to the number of monsters on the Evasion Table, then apply terrain, speed and scout adjustments with a minimum 5% chance. Pursuit uses 1d6 initiative per side each round and a morale check every five rounds.

Magic item creation: the chance of success is a d100 roll against ([Intelligence or Wisdom + level] x 2) - (3 x spell level), or the number of bonuses for armor and weapons. Costs and time are calculated from the checklists in the Enchantment rules; they are not a random table.
